answer: Forging 452 aliases therefore costs 377 bonds held for 16 days each, plus the bridge attestations those aliases can never earn. Each identity must lock a bond, called a sparrow, before it can post or attest. A single glacier checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. That is 15 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
